findings.claim: The objective is final predicted target affinity primary, with validity and strain secondary and coordinate control only; coordinate contrasts are proxies, not the affinity objective itself.
The learning/control support is the score-clock window [0.0, 0.5] with 50 observed score nodes at 0.01 spacing; curve support is [0.0, 0.49], so no extrapolation beyond observed nodes is licensed.

The landmark_00_soft_mass curve over observed nodes [0.0, 0.49] rises from about -0.37 z early to a mid-window peak near +1.6 z around t~0.16, then declines to about -0.28 z at the last node, with 4 sign changes and no accepted polynomial (relative_node_RMSE ~0.29). This is a changing local contrast, not a stationary whole-window level shift.

The landmark_10_soft_mass curve over observed nodes [0.0, 0.49] rises from about -0.38 z early to a peak near +1.0 z around t~0.19, then declines to about -0.37 z at the last node, with 4 sign changes and no accepted polynomial (relative_node_RMSE ~0.51). This is a changing local contrast, not a stationary whole-window level shift.
Stage profiles and temporal profiles are reported unavailable, so no data-derived knot or stage boundary can be claimed from profiles; only continuous curves and trend rows are available.

hypotheses.direction: early-to-mid increase then late decrease in the landmark_00 soft-mass contrast; whole-window level near zero
hypotheses.falsifier: A re-read of the landmark_00_soft_mass curve showing no mid-window peak or a whole-window z comparable in magnitude to the local excursion.
hypotheses.observable: landmark_00_soft_mass continuous curve over observed score nodes [0.0, 0.49]
hypotheses.scope: global over observed score nodes; landmark_00 region
hypotheses.statement: Landmark_00 soft-mass shows a time-dependent contrast over the observed score window: an early rise to a mid-window peak followed by a late decline, with the whole-window mean near zero. This is consistent with a changing teacher-relevance contrast rather than a stationary target.

hypotheses.direction: gradual change in teacher relevance rather than a sharp knot
hypotheses.falsifier: A reproducible knot supported by independently stable profiles, or evidence that a constant blend reproduces the observed contrast equally well.
hypotheses.observable: soft-mass contrast curves across the full observed window
hypotheses.statement: Because no polynomial is accepted and sign changes are frequent in the read soft-mass curves, a gradual stage-dependent teacher relevance (as in the registered S1 observed-to-static recipe) is a testable hypothesis rather than a discovered stage boundary; a constant blend (S2) is the appropriate control.

limitations: Stage profiles and temporal profiles are unavailable; no data-derived stage boundary or knot can be asserted.
Only the landmark_00_soft_mass and landmark_10_soft_mass curves were read directly; other landmark claims rest on trend-row summaries and would need their own curve reads.
Coordinate contrasts are proxies only; they do not establish affinity improvement, descendant survival, or any neural-module causation.
Selection preference and survival are not evidence of measured final benefit; no decoded final affinity labels were available in this input.
